subject: AuroraAI hosted pricing: monthly token runrate & 99th-tps follow-up
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Claire Ng <claire@aurora.ai>, Mike Torres <mike@aurora.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: AuroraAI hosted pricing: monthly token runrate & 99th-tps follow-up

Hi Claire / Mike —

Thanks again for the demo today — great conversation. As promised, quick post-call recap and the numbers I captured so we have a common baseline before I send a short MA and pricing band. Please correct anything that’s off.

Key asks / context (from AuroraAI):
- Primary workload: real-time summarization + retrieval-augmented chat for support. Average response ~ 140 tokens; full request+response ~ 180 tokens.
- Expected go-live in Q1 2027 with pilot traffic first 30 days.

Redwood hosted pricing qualification (your inputs + our interpretation):
- Current expected committed monthly token volume (starting): ~350,000,000 tokens/month (0.35B) — you indicated this could scale quickly with feature rollout.
- Target budget range: $4k — $10k / day initially (approx $120k — $300k / month) but you asked for a $/1M token view to compare unit economics.
- Target $/1M tokens (Aurora reference): looking for ~$15–20 per 1M tokens for hosted with a modest commit.
- Concurrency / peak TPS: sustained baseline 120 TPS; anticipated 99th-percentile spikes to ~420 TPS for short windows (1–5 minutes) during morning syncs. You noted occasional bursts up to 900 TPS during major incident replays.

Immediate next steps I’ll take:
1) Send a one-page Mutual Action plan + initial pricing band (attached) for 350M and an alternate 500M tier.
2) Share a sample hosted invoice and contract summary for procurement review.
3) Confirm SOC2 and data handling docs (we’ll attach links).

Attachments: AuroraAI_MA_draft_v1.pdf, aurora_pricing_band_v1.xlsx (pricing bands for 3 tiers).

If any of the baseline numbers above need to be adjusted (monthly token volume, average tokens per call, or the 99th TPS), flag them here and I’ll re-run the unit-econ view.

Thanks —
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AuroraAI hosted pricing: monthly token runrate & 99th-tps follow-up

Thanks Diego — quick clarifications from our side:
- Engineering revised the expected starting monthly token volume to ~420,000,000 tokens/month (0.42B). That’s with the initial feature set and conservative user growth.
- 99th percentile TPS we capture at 180 TPS under normal load; the 420 TPS number is closer to an *incident replay* window. We want pricing that tolerates short spikes (1–5 min) without elevation penalties.
- Budget: procurement wants a mid-point $/1M that lands near $16–18 for hosted but will evaluate total monthly spend against committed-term discounts.

Procurement asks before we engage legal:
1) Sample invoice / pricing summary (DocuSign-ready)
2) SOC2 attestation and a short data-retention summary
3) An explicit burst policy for hosted (how long and what capacity for free burst vs paid burst)

If you can send an updated MA with the 420M baseline and a 12-month commit option + a 3-month pilot option, we’ll prioritize review next week.

—Claire
Claire Ng
Head of Partnerships, AuroraAI

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Claire Ng <claire@aurora.ai>, Mike Torres <mike@aurora.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AuroraAI hosted pricing: monthly token runrate & 99th-tps follow-up

Claire — thanks, that’s helpful. I updated the MA and the pricing bands to reflect a 420M starter tier and an alternative 750M tier (attached: AuroraAI_pricing_final.xlsx).

Highlights / clarifications: 
- Unit pricing (hosted API, token-in+token-out) — proposed midpoint: $16.50 / 1M tokens for a 12-month commit at the 420M tier. 750M tier mid-point: $13.75 / 1M tokens.
- Pilot option: 3-month pilot at the 420M nominal tier with a 10% onboarding credit applied to month 1 spend (credit applied as invoice line item).
- Burst policy: we allow short bursts up to 5x baseline sustained TPS for windows <= 3 minutes without additional throttling. Anything beyond that falls into a short-term auto-throttle with immediate notification; sustained exceedance pushed to paid overage at the committed $/1M. We can formalize thresholds in the SOW.
- SLA / SOC2: SOC2 Type II report + data-retention summary attached as links (see related_links).

Additional commercial concession: We can extend a one-time 15% credit against the first full-month invoice if Aurora signs a 12-month committed plan within 30 days.

DocuSign (proposal + SOW): https://www.docusign.com/en/link/auroraai-proposal-1247
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deals/AUR-1247

Attachments: AuroraAI_pricing_final.xlsx (final banding), AuroraAI_MA_draft_v1.pdf (updated).

Let me know if you want a short call tomorrow to walk procurement through the invoice lines.

Best,
Diego
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
